utterances.text: Yes, sir, if you could stop here just for a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It is the last sentence, "I could not see the soldiers who shot at my brother". This is really --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: That is the relevant thing.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was facing the wall and I could not see over my shoulder.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Yes, sir. So what it says here is different from what Radoslav told you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I told you what he told me, and I am not competent for what is stated in this document. I know that this happened very shortly after we were transferred from the tunnel to number 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: All I am asking, and I am asking really because of our rules of evidence here, just asking for you to confirm for us that what Mr. Vujicic said in that statement is different from what he told you at Celebici; and that is just a yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Obviously it is different.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: That is fine, sir, that is all I was asking. Your Honour, I again move to admit that one paragraph plus the cover sheet and the signature page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Have you given a copy to the Registry?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: I believe it is on the witness stand, your Honour. I guess the Registrar can retrieve it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked D12/3.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Okay sir, let us go to a different subject here and let us see if we can get you out of here and home today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: With apologies to Madam Residovic. She has yet to take her turn.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, the look I just got ... Again, changing our subjects, in some of your statements, I think at least two and maybe three of your statements, you recounted an incident where some Arab journalists came through; do you remember the Arab journalists coming through?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: I will be right up front with you. Some of the witnesses here have testified that the Arab journalists actually filmed people being beaten in hangar 6 or at least in the camp and, as I recall, others testified that these Arab journalists actually took part in some of the beatings. Which one is it, sir, do you recall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They did not participate in the beatings, they did participate in the filming.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: So they just filmed the beatings, they did not join in, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They did not participate in the beatings, they just filmed the beatings.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: That is because other people have testified, I am trying to help clear that up, and I thank you very much for that, sir. Now I want to jump back again to a different subject. In your statement, the statement that you made to the District Court in Belgrade, you mentioned a woman named Grozdana Cecez; do you remember just generally about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Do you mean do I remember the woman called Grozdana Cecez, or do I remember making that statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Either one. Let us start off with: do you remember making the statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, certainly I made the statement, that was what we were talking about all afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Do you remember including in the statement, your statement, about Ms. Cecez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember. I do not know exactly what I said in that statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Okay. What I want you to do is help clear something up for me and it is this: in your statement made to the Belgrade Prosecutor you said that you heard Ms. Cecez being interviewed on a television programme. Do you remember seeing her on a television programme?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know what I stated, but I know that I did watch that interview. I do not know what the exact wording of that sentence is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: I would read it to you, but I wanted it in general terms. It is: "I heard from Grozdana herself when I saw her interviewed on Novica TV." Do you remember seeing her on television?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do remember seeing her speaking on television. The sentence is not very precise, not the moment when she was giving the interview but when the interview was being broadcast on television; not the moment of the interview, but the moment when it was shown on television.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: You just answered my next question, which was going to be, were you present when she was interviewed or did you just see it with everybody else in the world and you have just answered that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not present, I saw it on television. That is why I was saying the sentence is not precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: I understand that, sir, and that is why I ask you about it. You also said in your statement to the Prosecutor -- excuse me, to the court in Belgrade, same paragraph: "During the whole time" -- presumably that is the whole time that you were in Celebici -- "there were two women imprisoned in Celebici, but in another building. They were Grozdana Cecez from Donje Selo near Konjic and Milojka Antic from the village of Ibar, Konjic municipality." Do you remember making that statement, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Maybe you can help me with this, the year before on 18th February 1993 in Belgrade, where you gave a statement to a group called the Serbian Counsel Information Centre, you said in your statement: "There were no women in the camp at Celebici." Those are inconsistent statements, are they not, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the statements are inconsistent, they do not coincide, but please allow me to clear this up. May I be allowed to finish my sentence?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: If the Prosecutor wants to clear that up?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I will ask, your Honour, to allow the witness to finish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: He might be able to tell you why.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Can you clear up the inconsistencies between those two statements?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: These are facts which are available to the Trial Chamber, even without his clearing it, so let us hear him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Go ahead, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would be glad to and it is very simple to clear up. When I was asked whether women were imprisoned in Celebici, in the sense of large-scale imprisonment, similar to the imprisoning of men, hundreds and tens, I said then there were not any women because women were not imprisoned with us, either in the tunnel or in number 6. That was the sense in which I meant that there were no women, there was no massive incarceration of women at the Celebici camp. That is the inconsistency.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: So when you said there were no women, what you meant were there were only two women, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: So "no" means "a few"? Sir, let us go on to another subject. During the break, one of my co-counsels pointed something out to me that may not have been clear to them and they asked me to put this question to you so I will ask you this question: in Bradina, when you were arrested, the people that took you into custody were members of the army and not the guards at the camp, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The people who arrested us and forced us to climb the truck were men in uniform, but the system and the way in which we were loaded on to the truck with our hands behind our heads, looking down, without looking left or right, anyone who did got additional blows, so I cannot claim with any certainty that there may not have been guards in Bradina who were later guards at Celebici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: But it was not the guard force from Celebici that arrested you, it was the army that then transported you to Celebici, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said, I cannot answer that question with precision because the guards were wearing exactly the same uniform as the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Another thing, sir, is that in your evidence-in-chief, when Mr. Turone was asking you questions, you testified that Mr. Mucic was the commander at Musala; do you remember testifying to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Did you not say in your statements to the Serbian Information Centre, the one in February 1993, that a man named Ismet, I believe it is Hebibovic, was the commander at Musala?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Hebibovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Did you testify he was the Musala commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know how exactly it is stated. He was in Musala what Delic was in Konjic, but the commander of both camps together with Mr. Mucic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Did you not tell the Belgrade District Court in February or March 1994 that this same person was the commander at Musala?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the commander in the sense of everyday life, everyday organisation and checking of presence and being together with the guards, in the sense that Delic was the daily organiser of everything happening in Celebici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Sir, you are not familiar with the organisation charts for either one of those camps, are you? They did not share that with you, did they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they did not share it with us, but everybody knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: So everybody was just assuming, right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we were not assuming, it was not an assumption, we knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Because you had access to the Bosnian army orders assigning these people to things?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, certainly not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: One last thing, sir, and I believe this will finish us up and maybe get you out of here today, is --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I hope so too.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: I hope so too and I know you want to go back to your family and I appreciate that. Mr. Mucic accompanied you on the walk from tunnel number 9 to hangar number 6; do you remember testifying to that on direct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: You did not mention that in either one of your statements to either the Serbian Information Centre in Belgrade or the Serbian District Court, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not say that, because I repeat again that all the data that were collected were intended to collect the names of the people who were killed, who were beaten, and not to gather information on such details as to who accompanied us from the tunnel to number 6. Most of the people who were collecting that information felt that this was an insignificant detail, the simple transfer from one structure to another within the camp compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Sir, not wanting to argue with you, but I would just suggest to you that firstly the investigation before the District Court of Belgrade was a criminal investigation to find people to charge with offences, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know, I do not know whether it was criminal proceedings, I thought it was collecting information, so I am not familiar with the legal terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Well sir, I come from a very different legal system and I can be very wrong about that legal system too, but it seems that is what it says on the front. Would it surprise you, sir, that in that statement you have listed, in the English translation at least, almost two pages of people, a little less than two pages of people that you say were perpetrators of things? You list names like Osman Dedic, Padalovic, Kemo, Plosko, Turkovic. All those people were guards, were they not, at various places you were held custody?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the course of my testimony yesterday, I described in detail and with precision what I saw. As for the things that I did not personally observe, I did not mention them. Only what I saw or heard myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Your Honour, if I can go through my notes rather quickly, I think -- Scepo Gotovac, you testified about his death; you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Do you remember saying in your statements, at least in your statement to the District Court of Belgrade, that a 15 centimetre nail had been hammered into his forehead?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember stating that on the basis of the testimony of people who were right next to him. I said very clearly and with precision yesterday where I was and where he was and how much I could see from the position I held in the direction of the body of Scepo Gotovac as it lay there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Sir, I am from the United States and we are, I think, the last country in the world to still use feet and inches and miles and crazy things like that, so I am probably not as familiar with centimetres as I ought to me, but it seems to me 15 centimetres seems to be about that long (indicates). Your Honour, my daughter is much better at it, she is learning it at school. Sir, I thank you very much and I pass the witness, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Do you not think we should wait until tomorrow morning because we have now only five minutes left?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, it may be sufficient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you, wonderful.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good evening, Mr. R.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good evening, Madam -- Ms., I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: My name is Edina Residovic, I represent Mr. Zejnil Delalic, so that is sufficient for you to know during this evening, during our conversation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Fine, Madam.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Mr. R, I assume you must be very tired after very exhaustive examination and cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, rather.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. R, for having made so many statements before today's testimony and you were also spoke very extensively during the examination-in-chief and cross-examination, so that you even answered some questions several times, so that I, as the Defence counsel of Mr. Zejnil Delalic, have no questions for you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I never mentioned Mr. Delalic, as I know nothing about him, nor did I know him before the war, nor did I meet him anywhere during the war. Thank you too.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have no further questions for re-examination, but should I ask that the two previous statements to the investigating judge in Belgrade and to the OTP, be entered just to show the extent to which this witness has not been impeached through these two previous statements? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Let us know your reason for wanting to have it in. Let us have your argument.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would have no objection if it also includes the other statement we spent a long time talking about today, and that is the Serbian Counsel Information Centre. They have only offered two and all three should come.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I agree. Definitely we will be finding a way of bringing in a particular statement. If the statement has any relevance at all, then they should all come in.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: All right, your Honour. No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Let us have the statements. Have you any other questions, other than tendering those statements?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: Nothing else, you have already ruled, your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: The two statements were tendered and marked by Mr. Olujic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, we will find a clean copy of the third statement and deliver it to the Registry to be given whatever number it should be given by whoever it is given by.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: The last statement or all of them?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think there is a total of four statements involved in this, the one he gave to the Serbian Information Counsel, the one to the Serbian court, the one to the OTP and then Radoslav's statement. I have just been handed a clean copy of the last statement, I think we have got it solved, judge. If the usher can deliver this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Also mark this one so that we can know what its number is.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document will be marked D13/3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think this is the end of today's proceedings. Thank you, Mr. R. You have done very well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: May I be permitted to ask a question, if it is not out of order? I have a question to Mr. Olujic. I should like to see the document where it says that the cordon was 300 metres. Could I just see that line?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: These proceedings are over. I was only trying to thank you very much --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you and I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: -- and wish you very well on your voyage home. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: We have no proceedings tomorrow, and we are not likely to sit on Monday, because we have a plenary to attend.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: As your Honours please. There are no further witnesses available this week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Then we will keep our fingers crossed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: For next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes. As I said, we will not sit on Monday. We will meet on Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: (Court adjourned until 10.00 am on Tuesday, 21st October 1997)
